newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: A blend of profit-taking after bargain-hunting last week and futures-related dealings pushed industrial stocks gradually weaker on Tuesday to end near the day's lowest levels.
Gold stocks edged higher, losing some of their lustre towards the finish, as bullion juggled with the $349 level.
"The only positive today was the gold market. The fact that the gold price broke through the $349 level helped a lot," said one dealer.
But industrials were less fortunate, weighed further by concerns about possible inflationary pressures in the U.S. and the effect of this on the Dow.
"There was quite a bit of profit-taking. Institutions were pretty active last week snapping up bargains," a dealer said.
Arbitrage between the futures and underlying spot market also helped erode industrial shares, dealers said.

Volumes were moderate with dealers saying the day's turnover of around 700 million rand was deceptive as it was boosted by a few large deals. Notable of these was a 119 million rand asset swap in chemicals group Sasol Ltd and large bookovers in computer stock Persetel.

Another feature of the day was shares in oils and fuels group Engen which slid to their worst level in just short of a year following a profit warning on second half results announced at the release of interims on Monday.

"The negative is obviously the comment made that they don't think earnings will be any better in the second half...The market doesn't like companies with no growth in earnings," said Paul Carter, an analyst at ING Barings.
After ditching 1.5 percent to 22.75 rand, Engen stocks rose to end 10 cents firmer at 23.20 rand.
On the broader market the 100 percent industrial index ended down 40.9 points at 8,244.7, the gold index added 9.8 points to 1,327.8 and the overall index fell 30.6 to 7,044.1.
